answer: Scarcity-Proof Registry. Each identity must publish a unique sonnet whose every line encodes a hash of the previous line, and the registry accepts only one submission per sonnet root; duplicate roots are rejected at write time. An attacker who clones an identity must therefore compose a fresh sonnet for each clone, and any agent that tries to wander across registries with the same root is flagged, while the marginal cost per clone becomes one full composition plus a dune of verifier compute charged against the submitter.
